subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: PGP and Phil Zimmermann
description: A 60-second lesson on PGP and Phil Zimmermann.

hook.text: In 1991, Phil Zimmermann gave the world free encryption. The US government investigated him as an arms dealer.

buildup.text: Zimmermann created PGP — Pretty Good Privacy — to let anyone encrypt their email securely.

discovery.text: When PGP spread overseas, the government said Zimmermann exported munitions. Encryption was classified as a weapon.

twist.text: Zimmermann published the source code in a book. Exporting books was protected by the First Amendment.

climax.text: The case was dropped. Encryption became speech. One programmer changed the rules for everyone.

punchline.text: Code is speech. Encryption is a right.

quiz.question: Why was Phil Zimmermann investigated by the US government?
options: Because encryption was classified as a weapon and PGP spread overseas
Because he stole encryption algorithms from the NSA
